sections.h2: City or county: check which one you are in
sections.html:
Charlottesville is an independent city in central Virginia and the county seat of Albemarle County. The county surrounds the city on all sides, yet the two are separate governments with their own offices. A house with a Charlottesville mailing address can sit in the county, and most of the University of Virginia's grounds are legally in Albemarle County even though they feel like part of town.

That line decides who assesses your property, who issues permits and which zoning rules apply. Look at your tax bill first. The name at the top tells you which government you deal with, and it is worth settling before you talk to any buyer or agent.

The city has about 44,388 people in the 2025 Census Bureau estimate, down from 46,553 in the 2020 count, and the wider metro area has roughly 221,524.

Population measureCharlottesville
2020 census count46,553
2025 estimate44,388
Metro area (Albemarle, Fluvanna, Greene and Nelson counties plus the city)About 221,524
Land areaAbout 10.3 square miles

The town was founded in 1762 along Three Notched Road, which is the path of today's U.S. 250, and it grew into a rail town. Homes near Court Square and the old core were built long before the subdivisions on the edges, so repair needs differ a great deal from one street to the next.

When you contact us, the first thing we ask for is the year the house was built. A century-old house may have plaster walls, original wiring and a stone or brick foundation. A newer subdivision house is more likely to need a roof, HVAC or windows. Knowing which category you are in helps you decide whether to repair first or sell as it stands.

  • Older core: check wiring, plumbing, foundation and any exterior rules before you plan work.
  • Later subdivisions: check roof age, HVAC age and water around the foundation.
  • Either type: gather permits for past renovations so a buyer can see the work was approved.

sections.h2: Who buys and rents in Charlottesville
sections.html:
The University of Virginia and its health system anchor the job base, along with city government and the city school board, each at more than 1,000 employees. Only about 18 percent of people employed in the city live in it. About 82 percent commute in, and 42 percent of those commuters come from Albemarle County, while 11,497 city residents commute out.

In plain terms, a city seller competes with county houses for the same buyers. Pricing a city house as if the buyer must live inside the city limits tends to backfire.

  • More than 20,000 students come for the university each academic year, which lifts rental demand near campus.
  • University of Virginia Hospital and Martha Jefferson Hospital both serve the area.
  • Piedmont Virginia Community College has several locations in the city.

sections.h2: Weather and what it does to a house
sections.html:
Summers are hot and humid, winters are cool, and it rains in every month. July averages about 77.6 degrees and January about 36.2. The high passes 90 degrees on roughly 34 days a year, and snow averages 17 inches a season but rarely stays long. The wettest stretch runs from May through September.

That pattern puts the strain on air conditioning, attic ventilation, gutters and crawl spaces. A short walk-around before you sell saves surprises later.

  • Test the air conditioning and keep any service record you have.
  • Inspect the attic and the roof.
  • Look at the ground around the foundation for erosion or pooling after storms.
  • Check the crawl space for moisture.

Virginia's seller disclosure form tells buyers that the owner makes no statement about special flood hazard areas, dam break inundation zones, radon zones or marine clay soils. Buyers can research those on their own. A plain note from you about any past water problem builds trust and keeps the deal from stalling at inspection.

Interstate 64 and U.S. 29 are the main highways, with U.S. 250 and Route 20 also serving the city. I-64 runs east toward Richmond and west toward Staunton, and U.S. 29 runs northeast toward the Washington area and southwest toward Lynchburg. Charlottesville Area Transit runs city buses, JAUNT runs paratransit vans, and University Transit Service covers the campus area. The Amtrak station is served by the Cardinal three times a week, plus daily Crescent and Northeast Regional trains.

A house within walking distance of the Downtown Mall or a bus corridor appeals to renters and downsizers. A house outside the core appeals to buyers who drive. We weigh both when we put together a cash offer.

Charlottesville City Schools run six elementary schools, Walker Upper Elementary School, Buford Middle School and Charlottesville High School. Albemarle County Public Schools serve the surrounding county. If you are unsure which government covers your house, the school division on your child's records is one more clue, though some private schools with a Charlottesville postal address are actually in the county.

Call the city's planning and building offices and the treasurer to confirm any local requirement before you list, rent or renovate.

sections.h2: Costs and paperwork at a Virginia closing
sections.html:
On the deed, Virginia levies a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of the price. It lands on the seller by default, though a contract may hand it to the buyer. Part goes to the state and part to the locality, and Albemarle's circuit court clerk holds the deed until the money arrives. The rule is Virginia Code 58.1-802.

A tax bill left unpaid becomes a lien ranking above most others. At the settlement table, the closing agent clears it from what you would otherwise take home, and the contract decides how the current year's bill is split between you and the buyer. See Virginia Code 58.1-3340.

Sellers also hand over the Real Estate Board's residential property disclosure statement. On that form the owner declines to make any representation about historic district rules, lot lines, neighboring parcels, flood hazards, easements, lead plumbing, drywall or a dam's condition. From January 1, 2027, the statute adds a line about use-value assessment and roll-back taxes. Read Virginia Code 55.1-703 for the wording.

sections.h2: Selling for cash, step by step
sections.html:
Without a lender in the middle, nobody waits on an underwriter or an appraiser. What remains is the title work and your own paperwork.

  1. Send the address and a few details about condition and occupancy.
  2. We look at photos or visit, then put an offer in writing.
  3. After you say yes, the settlement company searches the land records for liens, judgments and unpaid taxes.
  4. Pick a closing day that suits your move, as long as the title search is finished by then.
  5. Sign the deed, and the proceeds follow once it is recorded.

People in town tend to call us about a parent's house after probate, a rental with a worn-out kitchen, or a job transfer that leaves little time. Nothing needs repairing or hauling away, because we buy the house as it stands. Turn the offer down and you owe nothing; listing with an agent is still open to you.

Pull together the deed, the latest tax bill, any loan payoff letter and, if the owner has died, the court papers naming who may sign. This page is general information about Charlottesville, not legal or tax advice, so confirm details with an attorney or the local government.

faqs.a: No. Charlottesville is an independent city and the county seat of Albemarle County, but the two are separate governments. Your tax bill and address records show which one covers your parcel.

faqs.q: How many people live in Charlottesville?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 46,553 people, and the 2025 estimate is 44,388.

faqs.q: What does Virginia charge a seller when a deed is recorded?
faqs.a: Under Virginia Code 58.1-802 the grantor pays 50 cents for each $500 of the sale price unless the contract moves some or all of it to the buyer. The clerk collects it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does Charlottesville get a lot of snow?
faqs.a: Snowfall averages about 17 inches a season, though it changes a lot year to year and rarely lingers. Summer is hot and humid, with about 34 days a year above 90 degrees.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Charlottesville without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Virginia's disclosure form leaves the buyer to do their own research, so you can sell as-is. You still give the buyer the Real Estate Board's disclosure statement.
